seoTitle: Business Insurance Cost for Cleaning Service Owners
seoDescription: Cleaning businesses pay about $305/yr for General Liability, $485 with E&O. See how janitorial bonds, theft allegations, and client property damage shape cost.

industryContext.contextNote: Cleaning businesses work inside clients' homes and offices with keys or access codes, making theft allegations and accidental property damage the dominant risk drivers.

riskFactors.title: Accidental Property Damage
riskFactors.description: Cleaning chemicals, equipment, or staff movement can damage flooring, furniture, or fixtures inside a client's property.

riskFactors.title: Theft & Missing Item Allegations
riskFactors.description: Because cleaners work unsupervised inside homes and offices, disputes over lost or damaged valuables are a leading source of claims.

riskFactors.title: Employee Injury On-Site
riskFactors.description: Slips, chemical exposure, and repetitive strain are common injury sources for cleaning crews working across multiple locations daily.

faqs.question: Why do cleaning businesses need a janitorial bond?
faqs.answer: A janitorial bond (fidelity/crime coverage) reimburses clients for theft committed by an employee, which General Liability does not cover and which clients often require before hiring.

faqs.question: What is the average cost of business insurance for a cleaning service?
faqs.answer: A cleaning service owner in the $0-50k revenue tier pays an estimated $305 per year for baseline General Liability coverage.

faqs.question: Does General Liability cover damage a cleaner causes to a client's home?
faqs.answer: Yes, General Liability typically covers accidental property damage caused during a cleaning job, such as a broken item or water damage from equipment.

faqs.question: Do cleaning businesses with employees need Workers' Compensation?
faqs.answer: Most states require Workers' Compensation once a cleaning business hires even one employee, given the physical nature of the work and injury frequency in the industry.

blogContent.whyThisRiskFactor: Cleaning service owners carry a 1.4 actuarial risk factor, reflecting frequent unsupervised access to client property and moderate physical injury exposure for staff.
blogContent.howCalculated: Premiums scale with revenue tier, crew size, and whether a janitorial bond or crime coverage endorsement is added to the base policy.
blogContent.comparisonNote: Cleaning service premiums are higher than office-based professional services but lower than skilled trades that involve power tools or structural work.
